content:
Following the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo this week, Apple has begun accepting trade-ins of the iPhone Air and iPhone 17 for credit. However, the iPhone Air trade-in deal is somewhat awkward, especially after this week's price hike.

Apple has typically waited until new iPhone models launch before accepting older devices for trade-in. But the iPhone Air and iPhone 17 are exceptions — there is currently no iPhone Air 2 or iPhone 18, and new versions are not expected until early next year at the earliest.

Nevertheless, Apple still wants iPhone Air and iPhone 17 users to have the opportunity to upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo. As a result, both models — which are currently still on sale by Apple without successors — are eligible for trade-in.

Taking the iPhone 17, which saw a $100 price hike this week with its starting price adjusted to $899, as an example, Apple offers up to $585 in trade-in credit.

The iPhone Air also saw a $100 price hike this week, with its starting price rising to $1,099. So for the $200 premium over the iPhone 17, what does the trade-in credit get you? The same $585. Truly astonishing.

Apple's trade-in value chart almost makes one suspect a $100 pricing error. In reality, Apple likely determines values based on market demand and component worth. Thinking about it further, the fact that the iPhone Air uses nearly the same chip as the iPhone 17 Pro is genuinely disappointing.

In summary, the iPhone Air has become $100 more expensive for new customers. Yet the iPhone Air's trade-in value, by Apple's standards at least, is on par with a model that costs $200 less. Seriously not great, Bob.
